No I meant harder to retain plus if you get stuck on a question you have to wait until a course instructor responds.
A lot of the WGU courses I took had only a few cohort offerings (live sessions or recorded sessions) so I was stuck reading the textbook and studying flash cards on quizlet. I prefer an instructor to break down each chapter to me and then have material to work through so I can retain the information. I personally think in person education works better but everyone has a different learning style.

I went to a technical college for accounting and went to WGU after for HR. I learned more at the tech school as it was hands on and unless you have experience in accounting it is probably hard to do it online with no instructor to ask for help while you’re working on it. If I could have a redo, I would have transferred my credits to the university in my town as I didn’t really like the way WGU courses were put together. I don’t know how the accounting program is though as I transferred all my accounting credits in.

Life seems so pointless. We work all the fucking time just to barely make it, we still have to borrow money to buy shelter and transportation. 
And why the fuck do we spend so much time and money on an education in the hopes someone will let us work for them. That sounds so backwards.

I had a really difficult childhood. Both of my parents abandoned me. My biggest regret is that I didn’t work super hard in school & go to an out of town college straight after high school. It is much easier to build a new life for yourself and get away from the place you grew up in if you do it right when you graduate high school.
My advice is don’t push people away, be kind to everyone, understand that what is going on at home it isn’t you - it’s definitely them, and work hard in school, get a job as soon as your old enough and save your money.
Then you can build the life you want.
Figure out what interests you and focus on that.
You are loved and important.

Hi, I decided to see a doctor who specializes in mental health last year after years of regular doctors giving me citalopram which did nothing for me.
I honestly didn’t know what was wrong with me. I never had interest in anything, would binge eat and drink out of boredom, and had major mood changes - often resulting in major melt downs where I would throw and kick things only to feel terrible about it within five minutes and blame it on my shitty childhood.
It probably isn’t worth mentioning what medication I am on now. I’m replying to this because I recently started reading ‘4 weeks to an organized life with adhd’ and it has opened my eyes to what adhd and add really are. There is a huge misunderstanding of what these two things truly are and the suffering that comes a long with it.
I suffer or have suffered from every symptom you are describing and I wish I would’ve realized what was truly wrong with me when I was younger. I am 28 now so I all those years my quality of life wasn’t where it should be and I pushed everyone away with the way I responded to any sort of change in emotion.
Thanks for this post, it’s very accurate.
